title: Prospective protocol for benign framing and task-contract robustness
evidence_boundary: This is a research handoff, not a preregistration, runnable benchmark, completed model study, or demonstrated attack mechanism. All experiments below are proposed. No empirical success rate, effect size, power, model ranking, or defense efficacy is reported.

inputs_and_rights: Author original synthetic tasks and framing variants with provenance and release permission; exclude private records and copied restricted benchmark prompts.

Use only an inference endpoint whose use is permitted for the planned study; separately verify model, dataset, and service terms. Publishing this protocol does not assert authorization for paid or third-party testing.
Do not redistribute third-party weights, transcripts, papers, or datasets merely because they are readable. Preserve exact raw and separately normalized local research text.
execution_boundary: No model execution is part of this release. No executable attack stimuli or runner is supplied by this protocol.
Future studies use benign contract-preserving requests; no jailbreak, rule-override, self-replication, persistence payload, external-action, or resource-exhaustion requests.
Primary studies disable tools and writable memory. Any later action study uses isolated local mocks with explicit allowed transitions.

resource_controls.accounting_rule: Before execution, set finite global request-attempt, output, time, and cost ceilings. The request-attempt ceiling covers all phases, models, replicas, retries, screenings, auxiliary judges, and recovery calls, including failed or uncertain attempts; workers must share it. Do not count only successful responses or reset the ceiling per retry.
resource_controls.comparability_rule: Compare conditions within a model under the same version, inference settings, task facts, output contract, available actions, and total per-case resource ceilings. Count defense overhead inside the same ceilings and report its actual use. Match input lengths per tokenizer where feasible and disclose residual imbalance; do not claim exact cross-tokenizer matching.
resource_controls.exhaustion_rule: Stop at a ceiling. Mark uninitiated scheduled cases NOT_ATTEMPTED and report the incomplete cohort; do not replace them selectively or enlarge the budget after seeing outcomes.

sampling_and_inference: Independently authored task/template origins define clusters; near-duplicate instances and repeated stochastic generations are nested observations, not independent tasks. Account for crossed template dependence when present.
Split development and evaluation by task/template origin. Do not use pilot or reviewed evaluation outcomes to optimize confirmatory prompts, thresholds, or model selection.
Randomize and balance condition order within task and collection-time blocks. Primary trials use fresh contexts; report model revisions and start a new cohort or stop if a revision changes.

Declare cluster/instance weights, primary endpoint, contrasts, multiplicity, and cluster-aware uncertainty before confirmation. Report per-model effects; a selected panel does not represent all models.

Pilot feasibility and clustered power or precision planning remain unperformed. Choose useful-effect and equivalence margins before confirmatory outcomes; statistical nonsignificance alone is not evidence of no meaningful effect.

outcome_accounting.primary_endpoint: Bounded task non-success per initiated evaluation case: a case succeeds only if it satisfies the fixed task contract under the resource policy.
outcome_accounting.case_denominator: All initiated cases remain counted, including refusal, empty return, truncation, timeout, transport/API error, and exhausted permitted recovery. Their causes remain separately labeled; transport errors are not model disobedience.
outcome_accounting.attempt_denominator: Report every attempted call, including failed and uncertain calls, with a parent case ID and retry/recovery role. Retries add attempts but do not add independent evaluation cases.
outcome_accounting.behavior_diagnostic: Contract violations among returned model responses retain refusals, empty messages, and truncated responses, scored against the contract with separate flags. No-output transport failures have unobserved model behavior. Report response availability and missing-outcome sensitivity bounds; do not call this selected subset the full causal effect.
outcome_accounting.first_attempt_and_recovery: Retain first-attempt outcomes and final bounded-policy outcomes separately. Recovery never overwrites an initial failure; define eligible transport retries before collection.
outcome_accounting.truncation_and_empty: Repetition metrics describe observed text only. A truncated prefix does not establish its unseen continuation; empty output has undefined normalized repetition coverage, not a successful zero-repetition score.
outcome_accounting.usage: Separate input tokens, visible output tokens, other reported billable tokens, grapheme length, bytes, and wall time. Missing usage is unknown rather than zero. A zero or missing baseline denominator makes a ratio undefined; report differences and availability instead.
outcome_accounting.ledger: Retain scheduled-case and linked-attempt identifiers, conditions, source/split, model/settings hashes, initiation status, finish reason, response flags, scorer result, observed usage, retry role, and missingness reason.

release_interpretation: A positive behavioral contrast would apply to the tested intervention and task distribution; it would not identify internal priority reordering or establish a novel attack class.
Repetition is a textual pattern, not automatically a contract violation, harmfulness, or server denial of service.
Negative and inconclusive results must be retained. Confirmatory claims require a separately frozen plan and completed authorized evaluation.

experiments.title: Semantic compassion and normative framing without repeated-symbol cues
experiments.question: Does benign compassion framing change bounded task non-success when task facts, authorization, output requirements, and repeated-symbol exposure are held fixed?
inputs: Original synthetic extraction, classification, or arithmetic tasks with deterministic correct answers and explicit contracts.
A 2x2 design: compassion present/absent crossed with normative framing present/absent; every condition has two fixed-position framing slots with matched neutral alternatives.
The semantic framing contains no emoji run, decorative repeated symbol, repetition instruction, or instruction to change the answer. Warmth is permitted only where the unchanged contract permits it.
A separate unaugmented task-only baseline and neutral-length diagnostic.
experiments.rights: Original synthetic inputs only; endpoint and release rights must be checked under global_rules.inputs_and_rights before collection.
baselines: The complete unchanged task with two neutral matched framing slots.
The task-only prompt, reported separately from the matched neutral control.
Within-model fixed decoding and deterministic contract scoring; generic added-text effects assessed by the neutral-length diagnostic.
experiments.resource_controls: Apply identical per-case ceilings and the shared global attempt cap. Match syntactic function and approximate per-model length without changing semantics; report remaining differences.
experiments.independent_units: Independently authored task/template clusters; instances and repeated draws nested within clusters. Hold out entire origins and report model versions separately.

outcomes.primary: Compassion main effect on the initiated-case bounded non-success endpoint.
outcomes.estimand: For fixed model m and prespecified cluster-weighted risks p_m(c,l), Delta_C=0.5*((p_m(1,0)-p_m(0,0))+(p_m(1,1)-p_m(0,1))).
secondary: Response-conditional contract violations, refusal/truncation/availability, output-token differences, and separately specified grapheme/token repetition metrics.
negative_controls: Legitimate warmth with unchanged correctness and format requirements.
Matched neutral added text and neutral-length variation.
Valid repeated data, empty responses, truncation, and transport failures in scorer fixtures; fixtures are not model results.

go_no_go.go_to_pilot: Proceed only after item review confirms equal answers, authorization and contracts; scoring is validated; rights, model settings and finite budget are fixed.
go_no_go.go_to_confirmation: Proceed only after a separate feasibility pilot supports a justified cluster-aware precision/power plan and prompts, splits, margins, scoring, multiplicity and missingness rules are frozen before new outcomes.
go_no_go.no_go: Stop for semantic mismatch, unreliable scoring, unresolved rights, insufficient resources for informative inference, model revision changes, or any external action outside scope.

experiments.interpretation: A signed framing contrast may indicate worse or better adherence. Nonsignificance is inconclusive unless prespecified equivalence is supported; neither direction proves a novel attack or internal mechanism.

experiments.title: Separate bounded repeated-symbol cue control
experiments.question: Can surface cue exposure or generic repetition priming account for an apparent framing-associated repetition effect?
inputs: A new held-out set preserving BF-01 task contracts.
Compare semantic framing without symbols against a separately controlled short symbol cue, with neutral-symbol and length-matched nonrepeating alternatives.

Cross semantic compassion presence with cue repetition where feasible; treat affective versus neutral symbol identity as a separate matched comparison rather than equating symbol identity with compassion.
The input cue is inert quoted data, strictly bounded before collection, and never asks the model to repeat, continue, copy, or propagate it. No cue strings are supplied here.
experiments.rights: Use original synthetic text and Unicode text symbols; no third-party artwork, protected prompt sets, or private transcripts are included.
baselines: Semantic compassion with no repeated symbols
Neutral framing with the same bounded surface cue
experiments.resource_controls: Freeze small cue lengths and symbol identities during development; equalize per-model input budgets where feasible, retain identical output caps, and count all attempts under the shared ceiling. Do not increase cue repetitions in response to failures.
experiments.independent_units: Independent task/template origins, with cue variants and stochastic draws nested; no recycling BF-01 evaluation outcomes to choose effective symbols.

outcomes.primary: Prespecified contrast separating semantic framing from surface repetition under the same task contract; exact statistical hierarchy remains to be frozen.
secondary: Observed grapheme repetition coverage with exact segmentation and interval rules
Per-model token repetition and output length
Input-copy overlap, refusal and truncation flags

go_no_go.go_to_pilot: Proceed only if cue identity, repetition, position, length, and semantic framing can be separated without changing the answer or inducing a request to repeat.
go_no_go.go_to_confirmation: Freeze new cue definitions, splits and analysis after development, using untouched evaluation origins.
go_no_go.no_go: Stop if semantic and surface cues cannot be meaningfully separated, cue text changes authorization, or the design requires escalating repetition or output budgets.

experiments.interpretation: A symbol-cue effect would support a surface-priming explanation in that design; it would not validate compassion as the cause. BF-01 and BF-02 are separate studies with separately qualified conclusions.
unresolved: Repetition metric parameters and implementation pin

experiments.title: Utility-preserving defense evaluation
experiments.question: Does an external validation or recovery policy reduce delivered contract violations while preserving legitimate task utility under the same total resource ceiling?
inputs: New held-out benign tasks and framing variants
Local synthetic mock state only if a tool extension is separately specified
experiments.rights: Use original synthetic items and properly licensed local components; any auxiliary model endpoint requires its own permitted-use check.
baselines: Undefended model with the same external hard budget
Individual defense components before a combined stack
experiments.resource_controls: Give each system the same total request, token, time and action ceilings; screening, judges, retries and recovery consume those ceilings. Report actual overhead and outcomes before and after intervention.
experiments.independent_units: Independent held-out task/template clusters; whole mock episodes are units for action evaluation, with repeated draws nested.

outcomes.primary: Joint prespecified decision criterion: lower delivered violations and retained task utility within a justified utility-loss margin.
negative_controls: Legitimate corrections that should be accepted

go_no_go.go_to_pilot: Proceed only when a useful baseline and external task scorer exist and defense overhead fits the shared ceilings.
go_no_go.go_to_confirmation: Freeze utility margins, decision rules, thresholds and component ablations on separate development data.
go_no_go.no_go: Reject a defense claim based only on refusing everything, hidden extra calls, excluded failures, or improved final formatting misrepresented as improved raw-model adherence.

experiments.interpretation: A filter may improve delivered output without changing the model. Any efficacy claim requires measured utility and full resource accounting; no efficacy has been demonstrated here.

experiments.title: Randomized-history carryover with fresh-context controls
experiments.question: Does a benign prior framing exposure alter the response to a later fixed target task when that exposure is absent from the target request?
inputs: Matched benign neutral-history and framing-history sequences
A separately specified, inspectable local toy-memory condition only if later justified
experiments.rights: Original synthetic histories and local synthetic state only; no user memory, private conversations, or third-party persistent systems.
baselines: Neutral prior history of matched difficulty, turn count and approximate length
Fresh context with no retained transcript or memory
An explicit memory-disabled control if a toy-memory arm is added
experiments.resource_controls: Charge prior histories and the target response to equal episode ceilings and the shared global cap. Keep target position, scoring and output limits fixed; inspect only declared local state.
experiments.independent_units: Independently authored whole conversation sequences clustered by task/template origin; individual turns are not independent repetitions.

outcomes.primary: Target-task non-success contrast between randomized matched histories, separately by transcript-retention condition.
secondary: Task correctness and bounded output repetition
negative_controls: State reset verified before each independent sequence

go_no_go.go_to_pilot: Proceed only when histories can be matched, the target is unchanged, and session/state reset is observable and controllable.
go_no_go.go_to_confirmation: Freeze sequence design, target position, state channels, contrasts and uncertainty analysis before collecting held-out sequences.
go_no_go.no_go: Stop if unexplained cross-session state or provider revision drift makes the randomized-history contrast uninterpretable. Do not introduce hidden persistence or cross-agent transmission mechanisms.

experiments.interpretation: A retained-transcript effect is causal context carryover under the randomized design, not weight modification or a persistent backdoor. Any toy-memory result is limited to its explicit storage channel; it implies no self-propagation.
unresolved: Whether a toy-memory arm is warranted
